Events

An event is the atomic unit of data that moves through a Pipeline. Every record a source connector emits, every row a transform produces, and every write a destination connector performs is an event.

Event shape

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=event.json|language=json|code={ "id": "evt_8f2c1a90", "type": "order.created", "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z", "source": "connector_postgres_orders", "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471", "amount_cents": 4899 } }}}

User data events vs. platform events

Godzilla distinguishes two kinds of events:

  • User data events — the records your pipelines process, shaped however your source system produces them.
  • Platform events — lifecycle notifications Godzilla itself emits: pipeline.started, pipeline.completed, pipeline.failed, connector.error. These are what power Webhooks.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Ordering|body_html=

Events are delivered in-order per source partition, not globally. Two events from different source partitions may be processed out of order relative to each other.

}}

Retries and dead-lettering

An event that fails a transform or destination write is retried with exponential backoff. After the configured retry limit, it is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped. See Handling errors & retries for how to configure and drain a dead-letter queue.

input.short_description: How event payload shapes are declared and validated in Godzilla pipelines.
input.body:
Schemas

A schema defines the structure, types, and constraints of the data in an event's payload. It acts as a contract between your source and destination systems, ensuring data integrity as it flows through a pipeline.

Why schemas matter

Schemas serve three critical functions:

  • Validation — Incoming events are checked against the schema before processing. Invalid events fail fast rather than corrupt your destination data.
  • Type safety — Explicit field types (string, number, boolean, timestamp, etc.) let connectors handle serialization and conversion correctly.
  • Documentation — The schema is a living record of what data your pipeline expects, visible to anyone building transforms or debugging issues.

Schema declaration

Schemas are declared in JSON Schema format and attached to a pipeline at configuration time. Every source connector has a schema field that describes the shape of events it will emit.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline.config.json|language=json|code={\n \"name\": \"ingest_orders\",\n \"source\": {\n \"connector_type\": \"postgres\",\n \"connection_id\": \"conn_prod_pg\",\n \"schema\": {\n \"type\": \"object\",\n \"properties\": {\n \"order_id\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n \"customer_id\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n \"amount_cents\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },\n \"created_at\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"format\": \"date-time\" },\n \"status\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"enum\": [\"pending\", \"completed\", \"failed\"] }\n },\n \"required\": [\"order_id\", \"customer_id\", \"amount_cents\"]\n }\n }\n}}}

In this example, the pipeline expects events with order_id, customer_id, and amount_cents as required fields, with status restricted to a fixed set of values.

Validation and error handling

When an event arrives that does not match the schema:

  • If a required field is missing, the event fails validation and enters the dead-letter queue.
  • If a field has the wrong type (e.g., a string where an integer is expected), the pipeline attempts coercion. If coercion fails, the event is dead-lettered.
  • If a field value violates a constraint (e.g., an enum value not in the allowed list), the event fails validation.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Dead-letter queues|body_html=

Failed validation does not retry. Invalid events go straight to your pipeline's dead-letter queue for manual inspection and replay. See Handling errors & retries for how to drain and replay them.

}}

Schema evolution

As your data sources change, you will need to evolve your schema. Godzilla allows you to:

  • Add optional fields — New fields with required: false do not break existing events.
  • Expand enum values — Add new allowed values to a constrained field without breaking old data.
  • Loosen type constraints — Relax a field from a specific type to a union type (though this requires a pipeline version bump).

Breaking changes — removing required fields, narrowing types, or shrinking enum values — require a new pipeline version and may require replay of older events under the new schema.

Common field types

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=common-types.json|language=json|code={\n \"string\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n \"email\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"format\": \"email\" },\n \"timestamp\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"format\": \"date-time\" },\n \"integer\": { \"type\": \"integer\" },\n \"decimal\": { \"type\": \"number\" },\n \"boolean\": { \"type\": \"boolean\" },\n \"array\": { \"type\": \"array\", \"items\": { \"type\": \"string\" } },\n \"object\": { \"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": { \"key\": { \"type\": \"string\" } } },\n \"enum\": { \"type\": \"string\", \"enum\": [\"active\", \"inactive\"] }\n}}}

For timestamps, always use format: "date-time" to ensure consistent parsing across connectors and transforms.

Relationship to Events

Every event flowing through a pipeline carries a payload field that must conform to the pipeline's schema. The schema is the definition; the payload is the instance. Understanding both concepts together is essential for building reliable pipelines.

input.body:
Events

An event is the atomic unit of data that moves through a Pipeline. Every record a source connector emits, every row a transform produces, and every write a destination connector performs is an event.

Event shape

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=event.json|language=json|code={\n \"id\": \"evt_8f2c1a90\",\n \"type\": \"order.created\",\n \"occurred_at\": \"2026-08-18T09:12:44Z\",\n \"source\": \"connector_postgres_orders\",\n \"payload\": { \"order_id\": \"ord_4471\", \"amount_cents\": 4899 }\n}}}

The payload field contains the actual data and must conform to the pipeline's schema. See Schemas for how payload structures are declared and validated.

User data events vs. platform events

Godzilla distinguishes two kinds of events:

  • User data events — the records your pipelines process, shaped however your source system produces them.
  • Platform events — lifecycle notifications Godzilla itself emits: pipeline.started, pipeline.completed, pipeline.failed, connector.error. These are what power Webhooks.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Ordering|body_html=

Events are delivered in-order per source partition, not globally. Two events from different source partitions may be processed out of order relative to each other.

}}

Retries and dead-lettering

An event that fails a transform or destination write is retried with exponential backoff. After the configured retry limit, it is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped. See Handling errors & retries for how to configure and drain a dead-letter queue.
